nodes.description: OER activation process in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The OER activity of the as-prepared NiSe₂ is tested in a standard three-electrode system by using 1 M KOH as the electrolyte. As shown in Figure 1b, the shape of the linear scan voltammetry (LSV) curves of NiSe₂ keeps changing with the continuous scans... At the steady state, NiSe₂ pre-catalyst also shows an excellent stability for over 20h and a nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency (Figure S2). The result from inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) demonstrates the Se:Ni atomic ratio of 0.0060 after the OER test, which is in accordance with that of 0.0051 from XPS

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH with different SeO₃²⁻ concentrations (optimum 0.1 M)
nodes.source_text: when 0.01M SeO₃²⁻ is added, the OER activity of Ni(OH)₂ is remarkably promoted... Compared with the Ni(OH)₂ in pure KOH, current density at the overpotential of 500mV (j₅₀₀) in the presence of 0.1M SeO₃²⁻ increases from 47 to 221 mA cm⁻² (Figure 2a). The decreased Tafel slope from 153 to 96 mV dec⁻¹ also indicates the promoted OER kinetics with the addition of SeO₃²⁻ (Figure 2b). ... The result from ICP-MS reveals that the Se loading on activated Ni(OH)₂ is 0.0133 mg cm⁻², much higher than that of Ni(OH)₂ only immersed in the mixture of KOH and 0.1M SeO₃²⁻ (0.00105 mg cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows flower-like structure assembled by porous nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image of the as-prepared NiSe₂ shows the flower-like structure assembled by porous nanosheets (Figure S1a)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows interplanar spacing of 2.44 Å attributed to (211) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the interplanar spacing of 2.44Å in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image is attributed to (211) facet of NiSe₂ (Figure S1b)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 853.2 and 870.4 eV for nickel selenide, 856.2 and 874.0 eV for nickel oxide; Se 3d peaks at 54.4 and 55.3 eV for selenide, new peak at 59.3 eV for oxidized Se after OER; Se atomic percentage decreases from 63% to 0.31%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p spectra of the as-prepared NiSe₂ (Figure 1c), the peaks centered at 853.2 and 870.4 eV can be assigned to nickel selenide ... After OER scanning, not only the atomic percentage of Se decreases from 63% to 0.31%, a new peak at 59.3 eV corresponding to oxidized Se also appears

nodes.characterization_summary: Se:Ni atomic ratio of 0.0060 after OER test for NiSe₂; Se loading on activated Ni(OH)₂ is 0.0133 mg cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The result from inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) demonstrates the Se:Ni atomic ratio of 0.0060 after the OER test ... The result from ICP-MS reveals that the Se loading on activated Ni(OH)₂ is 0.0133 mg cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe₂ shows peaks at 216 and 244 cm⁻¹ (Se-Se stretching); NiOOH peaks at 474 and 554 cm⁻¹ appear at 1.38 V; selenite (SeO₃²⁻) at 807 cm⁻¹ (1.23-1.53 V), selenate (SeO₄²⁻) at 834 cm⁻¹ from 1.53 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of the initial sample shows only two peaks at 216 and 244 cm⁻¹ ... The peak at 807 and 834 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to selenite (SeO₃²⁻) and selenate (SeO₄²⁻), respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Increased double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of NiSe₂ after OER test indicates higher ECSA due to Se leaching; C_dl values of Ni(OH)₂ with and without selenite are nearly the same.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The increased double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of NiSe₂ after the OER test (Figure S3) suggests that the Se leaching raises the electrochemical surface area (ECSA). ... The C_dl values of Ni(OH)₂ with and without selenite are nearly the same (Figure S6)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂ shows Ni-O at 452 cm⁻¹, NiOOH at 475 and 555 cm⁻¹ from 1.38 V; selenite at 807 cm⁻¹ initially, replaced by selenate at 834 cm⁻¹ at 1.58 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the region of 400-600 cm⁻¹, the peak at 452 cm⁻¹ at the beginning is attributed to Ni-O band in Ni(OH)₂ ... At 1.58 V, the peak at 807 cm⁻¹ is replaced by another peak of 834 cm⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: NiS₂ shows peaks at 272, 283, 475 cm⁻¹; NiOOH forms at 1.63 V; sulfite (SO₃²⁻) at 962 cm⁻¹ (0.93-1.43 V), sulfate (SO₄²⁻) at 981 cm⁻¹ from 1.43 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the corresponding in situ Raman spectra (Figure 4f), the peak at 272, 283 and 475 cm⁻¹ are attributed to T_g, E_g and A_g modes of NiS₂ ... The peak at 962 cm⁻¹ appeared from 0.93 to 1.43 V is assigned to sulfite (SO₃²⁻) Another new peak at 981 cm⁻¹ appears at 1.43 V, which can be indexed to the S-O stretch of sulfate (SO₄²⁻)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂ with sulfate shows surface-adsorbed sulfate promotion under OER conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The potential-dependent in situ Raman spectra (Figure 4h) and results from other electrochemical measurements (Figure S12-15 and Table S2) confirm that the surface-adsorbed sulfate can also promote the OER activity
